description: Unity UI Toolkit support boundary. Ordered; first match wins. Rules classify pointer families for the shapes the dispatcher admits (boolean form controls, select/toggle-item item groups, click-opened non-blocking anchored surfaces); whether a component is admitted at all is the dispatcher's decision, recorded per component in the capability inventory. `lowered` names what the emitter or shared C# runtime performs today; `pending` names the parity phase that will lower the family; `refused` states why UI Toolkit cannot realise the family idiomatically. Catch-all rules exist so that unknown prop families are never silently supported: an allowlisted component that reaches one fails generation until the family is adjudicated here.

phases.P2: Generic anatomy walker: ir.dom/ir.parts lower to a VisualElement tree; runtime bases become behaviors the generated constructor attaches.
phases.P3: Styling projection: generated USS from token facts, variants, states and box-model geometry; hand-authored palette removed.
phases.P4: Interaction families: static pressables, blocking and hover surfaces, composite and non-boolean form controls, month date grids, componentRef composition, messages, motion, typed C# declarations.
phases.P5: Corpus and admission: allowlist reaches the SwiftUI set; CI compile lane and committed-byte drift diff.

walker.ts (ProjectedText): the visible timestamp string becomes a generated Timestamp attribute painting its label.

rules.reason: Object-valued author/stats/embed data and the post id cannot be carried by UXML attributes; only the declared string leaves are projected and the object props are withheld rather than serialised.

rules.via: walker.ts (PageStrip): the presentation/progress axes become generated carrier properties.
walker.ts (PageStrip): the page labels become the generated Pages API the runtime builds one native button per label from.

rules.reason: The navigation label only feeds aria-label, which UI Toolkit does not populate; the page strip withholds it while the visible page labels stay consumer-authored.

rules.via: walker.ts (Otp): the field count, mode filter and read-only flag become generated attributes owned by OtpControl.
walker.ts (Otp)/OtpControl: the completion callback becomes a generated Completed action raised when every position is filled.

rules.reason: The group and per-field accessible labels only feed aria-label, which UI Toolkit does not populate; the runtime withholds them rather than faking an assistive tree.

rules.via: walker.ts (ChoiceGroup): the option array becomes the generated Options API over the nested option type, which the runtime translates to parallel leaf arrays for the native radios.

rules.reason: The HTML form-group name has no UI Toolkit counterpart and the group is not submitted with a form; the generated control withholds it.

rules.via: walker.ts (Select): the option array becomes the generated Options API over the nested option type translated to parallel leaf arrays.
walker.ts (Select): the placeholder becomes the generated Placeholder attribute painted by the trigger label when no option matches.

rules.reason: Multi-select, custom filtering, searchable mode and the empty-state flag exceed the single-selection runtime; they are withheld rather than approximated.
The trigger and search accessible labels only feed aria attributes with no UI Toolkit consumer; they are withheld.

rules.via: walker.ts (Expansion): both state-dependent labels become generated carrier attributes painted by the runtime.

rules.reason: Line clamping needs text measurement the expansion runtime does not own; the max-lines presentation is withheld rather than approximated.

rules.via: walker.ts (Expansion): the expandable switch and both state-dependent labels become generated carrier attributes painted by the runtime.
walker.ts (PagedSet): the page labels, declared count and disabled flag become the generated Pages/PageCount/Disabled attributes backed by PagedSetControl.

rules.reason: The composed page-choice presentation requires instantiating the admitted Pagination child, which the paged navigator runtime does not own; both knobs are withheld.
The accessible labels only feed aria attributes with no UI Toolkit consumer; the runtime builds unlabelled native controls and withholds the labels.
Prop families not yet adjudicated for UI Toolkit. An allowlisted component may not rely on this rule: add a family rule above.

rules.via: walker.ts (Coachmark): the numeric step channel is exposed as a generated int UXML attribute the consumer manages; no controlled/request semantics are claimed.

walker.ts (Select)/SelectControl: the open channel is exposed as the generated Open/DefaultOpen API with OpenChanged/OpenRequested semantics; the selected-channel realisation check covers the selection channel only.

walker.ts (Transfer)/TransferControl: the selection channel is exposed as a plain string[] API with commit/request semantics; the selected-channel attribute realisation does not apply to array channels.

The one channel the dispatcher selects maps its value/default/change trio to the C# value property, pre-attachment assignment and change callback or event; Controlled + ValueRequested carry owner-controlled state. A second channel is unrealised and refuses generation.
walker.ts (ChoiceGroup): the orientation union vocabulary backs the generated orientation carrier attribute.
walker.ts (Select): the option alias backs the generated nested option type and the size union backs the generated size carrier attribute.

rules.reason: The trigger/search accessible message strings need the P4 message/a11y family; the visible placeholder and option labels remain consumer-authored.
Named types lower to C# string/bool today; enums, unions and records need typed C# declarations.

rules.via: uss.ts (S4): a variant predicate lowers to the class-recipe modifier carrier .<cssPrefix>--<value> on the root or as the part's ancestor; the walker emits the axis as a [UxmlAttribute] when a behavior knob consumes it or a carrier exists. A modifier with no Unity carrier is listed uss-selector in Controls.unsupported.json.

uss.ts (S4): a state predicate lowers to the behavior's state class at its placement (host for BooleanControl and AnchoredSurface, paired parts for ItemGroup), to native :hover/:active/:focus/:disabled, or to BooleanControl's mirrored is-hover/is-active/is-focus host classes; what USS cannot select is listed in Controls.unsupported.json (uss-pseudo, uss-owner-mismatch, uss-floating-scope).

rules.reason: USS has no @keyframes; it supports property transitions only. Keyframe animation would need a scheduler-driven C# runtime, which is not an idiomatic lowering of a stylesheet fact.
USS transitions, loops and reduced-motion gating are not generated yet.

rules.via: Events emitted through the selected channel's change prop surface as RegisterValueChangedCallback (boolean) or the ValueChanged C# event (selection); C# signatures use arrays for both selection modes. Any other event is unrealised and refuses generation.

rules.reason: Transitions are implemented by hand in ItemGroup and AnchoredSurface; there is no generic state-machine lowering.
No HTML form participation, constraint validation or field association exists in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches the BooleanControl behavior for boolean value models (R7).
The dispatcher attaches the TextInput behavior for a text value model whose form-control part is the input root; the generated class derives the native TextField (R7).
The form-control part renders as the Button BooleanControl.Attach binds (exposed as Trigger); the channel selects the generated C# value property and constants.
BooleanControl commits on trigger activation, which is the change moment of a boolean control; there is no intermediate input phase to defer.
BooleanControl.Attach binds the control's native Button.clicked event, which is the activation commit the contract declares; no separate change event is emitted.
TextControl commits on the native text change event of the child input that the wrapper exposes.
TextControl commits on the native text change event, which is the input-committed update the contract declares for a root input control.

walker.ts (Select)/SelectControl: the collection-selection model is realised as a single-selection runtime listbox with activation commit and listbox closing; multi-select update semantics are withheld.

rules.reason: Composite controls (Select, RadioGroup, …) need a composite runtime behavior; the dispatcher rejects them today.
A month date grid (Calendar) needs a date-grid runtime behavior: locale-formatted weeks, roving focus over gridcells and the value and month channels; the dispatcher rejects it today.

rules.via: walker.ts (Transfer)/TransferControl: the declared transfer value channel and options prop drive the runtime dual-list derivation.
behaviors.ts (Modal / AnchoredSurface): a close trigger's native activation requests the closed value; ModalSurface wires the close button to the open channel.

The dispatcher attaches ItemGroup for select / toggle-item, AnchoredSurface for toggle with a surface (click mode) or open (hover/focus-open mode), and Disclosure for a surface-less toggle whose single trigger owns one presence-tracked content part; ItemGroup.Attach(…, operation, …) carries the operation into the runtime.

The trigger and content parts are generated keyed sub-elements (R4) the attached behavior discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class; the channel selects the generated value property and constants.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Disabled and gates activation through SetEnabled.

The dispatcher admits hidden only on ItemGroup (inactive content hidden, detached when UnmountInactive is set) and unmount only on AnchoredSurface (floating content removed on close); other pairings are refused.

rules.reason: The declared clamp presence needs text measurement the expansion runtime does not own; the runtime toggles the state class but does not clamp the content.

rules.via: ItemGroup.Attach(…, orientation, wrap) initialises arrow-key orientation and wrapping; declared orientation / loop props override them through the item-group vocabulary.

The dispatcher pairs each strategy with the behavior that realises it and refuses other pairings (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_FOCUS): roving and manual on ItemGroup (passed to Attach; arrow / Home / End navigation), auto on BooleanControl (native Button focus), none on AnchoredSurface (no trap; focus stays on the trigger or moves into the content).

rules.reason: The initial focus target is not read. ItemGroup's roving tabIndex makes the active tab, or every trigger, the first tab stop regardless of the declared part; a declared target that differs would be ignored.
Prose description of the focus strategy; documentation only.

rules.via: behaviors.ts (Modal): ModalSurface traps Tab/Shift+Tab inside the content while open and returns focus to the previously focused element on close; no focus-visible distinction exists in UI Toolkit.

rules.reason: DOM focus-target ids and page scroll-lock have no native counterpart for the modal runtime; they stay pending P4 and the generated control exposes no property for them.

rules.via: AnchoredSurface reparents floating content to the panel root and re-attaches the stylesheet; the dispatcher refuses any non-surface shape that enables a portal (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_PORTAL).
Content stays in the document tree; the dispatcher refuses an anchored surface whose portal is disabled because AnchoredSurface always reparents (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).
The panel root is the UI Toolkit equivalent of document.body.
AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger's world bound and flips/shifts at panel edges.

rules.reason: USS has no z-index: UI Toolkit orders siblings by hierarchy and AnchoredSurface brings floating content to the front of the panel root, so named layers have no USS realisation.

rules.via: behaviors.ts (Modal): ModalSurface portals the host to the panel root and renders the contract's backdrop as the overlay; the modality gate prop is consumed by the selected blocking mode.
behaviors.ts (Toast): ToastSurface portals the host to the panel root and anchors it to the viewport edge; no backdrop is drawn for an ephemeral non-blocking surface.
behaviors.ts (Modal): ModalSurface realises escape and backdrop-click dismissal through generated CloseOn* knobs and close-button dismissal through the trigger's native activation.

behaviors.ts (Modal): the declared escape/overlay/close-button dismissal triggers become the generated CloseOn* knobs and the trigger's native close activation; enabledBy props gate the knobs' defaults.
AnchoredSurface CloseOnEscape / CloseOnOutsideClick / CloseOnBlur over the anchor/content union; hover mode closes on pointer leave when the surface declares it.
The named prop is emitted as the matching [UxmlAttribute] CloseOn* flag.
An empty trigger list declares no dismissal; the attached behaviors register none.
behaviors.ts (Toast): timeout dismissal runs through the auto-dismiss timer, Escape through the host key handler and close-button through the close control's native activation.

rules.reason: pointer-leave, close-button and other dismissal triggers need the blocking and hover surface behaviors and an explicit decision here.

rules.via: Click mode toggles on the trigger Button's clicked event; the hover/focus open mode listens for pointer enter and focus on the trigger and closes on pointer leave.
The anchor and content parts are generated sub-elements (R1, R4) AnchoredSurface.Attach discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class.

behaviors.ts (Modal): a centered, persistent, viewport-attached blocking dialog surface lowers to ModalSurface, which portals the host, fills the panel, centers the content and renders the overlay backdrop.

behaviors.ts (Toast): an ephemeral non-blocking viewport-edge toast lowers to ToastSurface, which portals the host, anchors it to the viewport edge, toggles the item's presence and owns the auto-dismiss timer from the declared timing prop.
Interactive surface content is a generated focusable sub-element (R1); non-interactive content (tooltip) is generated non-focusable and the hover mode never focus-traps it.

rules.reason: aria-controls / aria-expanded relations have no assistive-technology consumer in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher admits part-anchored popovers and tooltips only; AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger and flips/shifts at panel edges.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Placement and drives Reposition.

rules.reason: Id-referenced ARIA relationships; UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree that could consume them.

rules.via: ItemGroup arrow / Home / End navigation and native Button submit activation (Space / Enter) through NavigationSubmitEvent; a keyboard declaration on a contract with no channel and no projected action root is not lowered by this claim.

rules.reason: Roles, labels and ARIA attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree on desktop, and Unity's mobile AccessibilityHierarchy is not populated by UI Toolkit. Revisit when that integration exists.
The list/button accessible message strings need the P4 message/a11y family; visible row labels are the option ids and the buttons stay unlabelled.
The show-more/show-less message defaults need the P4 message family; the label attributes stay consumer-authored.
The component message catalog is not lowered for Unity; generated controls carry no localisable text.
Truncation policy needs USS text-overflow projection and a measuring runtime.
Sequence and paged-set position policies need their own runtime behavior.
UI Toolkit has no CSS grid layout; uss.ts lists a grid display declaration as uss-scalar instead of treating it as a flexbox equivalent.
USS has no grid-template-rows or animated grid track sizing; uss.ts lists the declaration as uss-property.

The USS property table (uss.ts) has no lowering for these CSS properties: USS (Unity 6000.5) has no box-shadow, line-height, keyframe animation, contain, clip or CSS text-transform; draw order is visual-tree order, not z-index; picking is VisualElement.pickingMode, set from C#, not pointer-events; -unity-text-align couples both axes where CSS text-align controls only the horizontal axis; a CSS font-family list has no source-bound native font asset. Each declaration is listed uss-property in Controls.unsupported.json.

uss.ts maps no CSS cursor keyword: a runtime USS cursor is a texture with a hotspot, which the contract does not carry (USS's named cursors apply in the Editor only). Each declaration is listed uss-scalar.
uss.ts paints a focus outline as the element's own border, which cannot stand off the box; only a zero offset is realised. Each other offset is listed uss-property.

-unity-font-style carries bold and normal only; an intermediate weight (100-300, 500) needs a font asset per weight, which the token graph does not carry. Classified by the declared value; uss.ts decides a token-fed weight by the token's value in every theme and brand scope, and Controls.unsupported.json records that outcome (uss-scalar, or uss-var-composite when the scopes disagree).

A USS transition names USS properties and a keyword easing: a transition of transform (USS splits it into translate, rotate and scale) or with a cubic-bezier, steps or token-fed easing does not carry its CSS meaning. uss.ts keeps the realisable parts (properties, durations, ease) and lists the rest under the transition's longhand in Controls.unsupported.json.
USS lengths are px or % literals; calc() has no USS form and uss.ts does not evaluate it. Each declaration is listed uss-scalar.
An em length depends on the computed font size of its parent; the fixed-root rem conversion cannot preserve that relative value. The USS projection lists it uss-scalar.
USS does not accept currentColor as a color scalar. The glyph renderer inherits its host's resolved foreground instead; uss.ts records the authored declaration as uss-scalar.

A component slot is defined only with one USS scalar (length, percentage, number, time, angle, colour, keyword, a rem value resolved against the fixed 16px native root, or a var() with a scalar fallback). A multi-component value (shadow list, two-value padding, font-family list), an easing function or an unresolved relative unit (em, ch, vw, vh) has no USS custom-property form uss.ts emits; each definition is listed uss-scalar.
The dismissal style selectors target the omitted guarded chrome; P4 composition re-enables the action control and its state styles.

The IR's native style grammar refuses the selector key (an attribute or ARIA state such as [aria-expanded], a web-template state class such as <part>--active, a combinator, or a structural pseudo-class), so no native style rule exists for USS to lower and uss.ts lists the key uss-selector. The IR-facts spec that carries these states as contract state predicates precedes P4, which lowers them.

rules.via: uss.ts (S2/S3): token bindings become component custom properties var(--fsds-<graph path>, <fallback>) over a generated token section (.fsds-theme light, .fsds-theme--dark, .fsds-brand-<id>) projected from resolved.tokens.json and the token build's @layer brand.

rules.reason: The USS projection has no transition-duration/transition-timing-function, transition-property, text-decoration, aspect-ratio, border-collapse, overflow-axis, tab-size, order, inset or overflow-wrap handler and USS has no user-select, list-style-type or list-style property; the projection lists each such declaration uss-property in Controls.unsupported.json.
The fixed-root projection does not carry CSS keyword inheritance for a component declaration; the projection lists the declaration uss-scalar.
USS white-space supports only normal/nowrap; the projection lists the declaration uss-scalar and the passive lowering does not approximate it.
Fixed intrinsic media geometry resolves through authored relative lengths the native texture element does not carry; the declarations are ledgered uss-scalar pending the P4 sizing family.
USS has no object-fit/object-position; the native Image element exposes only low-level scale/source-rect primitives that the generated media API does not claim.
The select modifier descendant selectors pair authored state classes with trigger descendants the generated stylesheet cannot compose; the declarations are withheld rather than emitted partially.

The presentation-modifier descendant selectors pair a carrier class with a runtime-built item class, which the authored-selector projection does not compose; the declarations are withheld from the stylesheet rather than emitted partially.

A modifier-block height resolves through the typography ramp to a relative rem value the fixed-root projection does not carry for non-typography geometry; the projection lists the declaration uss-scalar.
USS has no intrinsic sizing keywords; the projection lists these declarations uss-scalar in Controls.unsupported.json.

A modifier class qualified by a web-template pointer state has no native style rule: the runtime adds no such state class and uss.ts lists the key uss-selector. The P4 state-style family carries these states.
USS has no pseudo-elements; the projection lists every declaration of such a selector key uss-pseudo-element.
The web indeterminate (mixed) pseudo-class has no Unity state; the projection lists its declarations uss-pseudo.

Viewport units, min()/max()/calc() length expressions and other relative viewport sizing are not projected; the projection lists the declaration uss-scalar, and the modal runtime owns the blocking layout.
UI Toolkit has no fixed/sticky positioning; the projection lists the declaration uss-scalar and ModalSurface sets its own absolute blocking layout.
The invalid state variable has no native carrier on the generated text field; its declarations wait on the P4 state-carrier family and are ledgered pending.
The invalid state has no native carrier on the generated text field; its modifier-state selectors wait on the P4 state-carrier family and are ledgered pending.
The transfer list min-size presentations depend on the authored list markup the runtime recreates without those size slots; they are withheld rather than emitted partially.
The web line-clamp presentation and its expanded reset are not expressible in the native text grammar; they are withheld rather than emitted partially.
The authored trigger background is not projected onto the native button chrome; the declaration is withheld rather than emitted partially.
The web line-clamp presentation and its expanded reset are not expressible in the native text grammar; they are withheld rather than emitted partially.
Tabular-figure numerals are not expressible in the native text grammar; the context declaration is withheld rather than emitted partially.

rules.via: uss.ts (S3-S5): each native style rule becomes one USS rule through the CSS-to-USS property table (gap lowers to --fsds-gap, realised by the runtime Gap helper; a composed-content host restates its owner's container declarations); a declaration USS cannot realise is listed with its reason in Controls.unsupported.json, generated beside Controls.uss.
